title: Word2Vec vs. GloVe vs. GPT vs. BERT... oh my!

cues.en: Welcome to this section of the course, which is all about embedding spaces, embedding matrices and embeddings vectors.
cues.zh: 歡迎來到這一章，主題是嵌入空間、嵌入矩陣與嵌入向量。

cues.en: In this section, we are going to focus more on importing, working with and creating embeddings vectors.
cues.zh: 這一章會著重匯入、使用與建立嵌入向量。

cues.en: Now there are many word embeddings.
cues.zh: 詞嵌入有很多種，

cues.en: Matrices that are designed for different purposes, come from different research groups, or different
cues.zh: 不同的矩陣為不同目的設計，來自不同研究團隊或

cues.en: companies, are constructed based on different algorithms and have different goals.
cues.zh: 公司，以不同演算法建立，目標也不同。

cues.en: So in this lecture, I'm going to start with a reminder of what word embeddings are.
cues.zh: 這一講先複習什麼是詞嵌入，

cues.en: And then I will provide a brief introduction to four of the more popular embeddings matrices that we will explore and work with in this course.
cues.zh: 再簡單介紹四種較常見、本課程會探索與使用的嵌入矩陣。

cues.en: Now embeddings vectors are really foundational to language models.
cues.zh: 嵌入向量是語言模型非常根本的基礎。

cues.en: In fact, even the most sophisticated language model is basically just working with embeddings vectors in sophisticated ways.
cues.zh: 事實上，即使最先進的語言模型，基本上也是以複雜方式操作嵌入向量。

cues.en: So this slide is a repeat of what you saw in the beginning of the previous section.
cues.zh: 這張投影片，在上一章開頭看過。

cues.en: I want to go through this slide again briskly to remind you of the idea of what embeddings are.
cues.zh: 我想快速再說一次，複習嵌入的概念。

cues.en: So the idea is that words as represented by letters or as integers in a one hot encoding scheme are
cues.zh: 概念是，以字母，或以獨熱編碼方案中的整數表示的單字，

cues.en: completely separate from each other, with no relationship across each other.
cues.zh: 彼此完全分離，沒有關係。

cues.en: But on the other hand, the real world objects that these words refer to do have meaningful relationships.
cues.zh: 但這些單字指涉的真實世界事物，卻有有意義的關聯。

cues.en: For example, the words cat and dog have nothing whatsoever to do with each other.
cues.zh: 例如，cat 與 dog 這兩個單字，本身毫無關係。

cues.en: They don't even share the same letters with each other.
cues.zh: 甚至連字母都不相同。

cues.en: But the thing that the word dog refers to in the real world has a lot of meaningful semantic relationships
cues.zh: 但 dog 這個字在真實世界中指的事物，與

cues.en: with the thing that the world that the word cat refers to.
cues.zh: cat 所指的事物，有許多有意義的語意關係。

cues.en: Now, if we were to just represent language as a collection of individual words, we wouldn't be able to capture all of those meaningful real world relationships.
cues.zh: 若只把語言表示成一組獨立單字，就無法捕捉那些真實世界中的有意義關係。

cues.en: So instead, the idea is to use continuous numerical spaces to represent all of these words according
cues.zh: 因此，改用連續的數值空間，依照這些字

cues.en: to properties of the things that these words refer to.
cues.zh: 所指事物的屬性，表示各個單字。

cues.en: So the real world objects that are dogs and the real world objects that are cats are related to each
cues.zh: 真實世界中的狗與貓，彼此有關，

cues.en: other in that they are approximately the same size and approximately the same friendliness.
cues.zh: 例如體型大致相近，友善程度也大致相近。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: That's just for simplicity.
cues.zh: 這只是為了簡化，

cues.en: Let's just leave it at that.
cues.zh: 就先這樣說。

cues.en: Now, that fact is not apparent when looking at these two sets of three letters.
cues.zh: 只看這兩組各三個字母，並不會看出這件事。

cues.en: But when we plot the words in this embeddings space, then we actually can quantify how these words are related to each other.
cues.zh: 但把單字畫在嵌入空間中，就能量化彼此的關係。

cues.en: So that's the motivation for embeddings.
cues.zh: 這就是嵌入的動機。

cues.en: And this is a really simple hand-crafted toy example.
cues.zh: 這只是非常簡單、手動設計的小型範例。

cues.en: Actual embedding matrices that are used for research and commercial applications in natural language
cues.zh: 自然語言處理研究與商業應用中的真正嵌入

cues.en: processing are much higher dimensional, and generally the axes are not human interpretable in the sense
cues.zh: 矩陣，維度高得多，而且座標軸通常無法人類解讀，

cues.en: that it's not really possible to label an axis as corresponding to size or friendliness.
cues.zh: 也就是無法直接把某條軸標成體型或友善程度。

cues.en: You will see in the next section of the course that we will try to do some analysis to extract labeled
cues.zh: 下一章，會嘗試透過分析，在高維空間中擷取可標示、

cues.en: and interpretable axes within these high dimensional spaces, but that doesn't really work so well except
cues.zh: 可解讀的軸，但除了少數值得注意的例子，效果並不好，

cues.en: for a few noteworthy examples, and that's really more the exception than the rule.
cues.zh: 而且，那些比較像例外，並非常態。

cues.en: So this statement here modified during model calculations that is true for language models like GPT
cues.zh: 這裡所說「在模型計算中修改」，對 GPT、

cues.en: and Bert, but it's not generally true for all embeddings matrices.
cues.zh: BERT 等語言模型成立，但不是所有嵌入矩陣都如此。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: I keep using this word matrices, but so far I've only been showing vectors.
cues.zh: 我一直使用「矩陣」這個詞，但目前只展示向量。

cues.en: So what are embeddings matrices and how do they relate to vectors.
cues.zh: 嵌入矩陣是什麼？和向量有什麼關係？

cues.en: So the idea is that we take all of the individual vectors for individual words, and then we concatenate them to create one big matrix.
cues.zh: 概念是，取出每個單字的個別向量，再接起來，建立一個大型矩陣。

cues.en: So this matrix has words or tokens by embedding dimensions.
cues.zh: 矩陣的大小是單字或 token 數，乘以嵌入維度。

cues.en: Now different embeddings matrices that are created by different research groups or companies have different sizes.
cues.zh: 不同研究團隊或公司建立的嵌入矩陣，大小不同。

cues.en: But in general, the number of tokens or words varies between tens or hundreds of thousands, and the
cues.zh: 不過，一般而言，token 或單字數大約是數萬到數十萬，

cues.en: number of embeddings dimensions varies between hundreds to a couple thousand.
cues.zh: 嵌入維度則從數百到數千。

cues.en: So you can compare that to this cute little set over here which has five words and two dimensions.
cues.zh: 可以和這裡可愛的小型例子比較，它只有五個字、兩個維度。

cues.en: Now, why would we want to store all of these individual vectors in a matrix?
cues.zh: 為什麼要把所有個別向量，存進矩陣？

cues.en: In fact, this is done purely for practical purposes.
cues.zh: 其實，純粹是實作上的考量。

cues.en: During language modeling, we actually look up the individual vector that's associated with each token and pluck that out of the matrix.
cues.zh: 語言建模時，會查找各 token 對應的個別向量，再從矩陣取出。

cues.en: So storing everything in a matrix is really just for simplicity of calculations and code.
cues.zh: 所以，全部存在矩陣裡，只是為了簡化計算與程式。

cues.en: So we do work with the embeddings matrices.
cues.zh: 我們確實會操作嵌入矩陣，

cues.en: But usually you're thinking about this not as a full matrix but as a collection of individual vectors.
cues.zh: 但通常把它想成個別向量的集合，而不是一整個矩陣。

cues.en: But how do we even get all of these individual vectors?
cues.zh: 不過，這些個別向量從哪裡來？

cues.en: How do we define the numbers in these vectors?
cues.zh: 向量裡的數字，如何定義？

cues.en: Well, they are learned from data, as you will see later in this section.
cues.zh: 它們從資料中學得，這一章稍後就會看到。

cues.en: But there isn't just one single embeddings matrix as I mentioned at the beginning of this lecture.
cues.zh: 但如本講開頭所說，嵌入矩陣不是只有一個。

cues.en: There are many embeddings matrices.
cues.zh: 有很多不同的嵌入矩陣，

cues.en: You can even create your own matrix if you want.
cues.zh: 如果願意，甚至可以自己建立。

cues.en: In this section I will introduce you to four embeddings matrices.
cues.zh: 這一章，會介紹四種嵌入矩陣。

cues.en: Although for the rest of the course we're really only going to focus on embeddings matrices that are built into llms like GPT.
cues.zh: 但接下來的課程，主要著重 GPT 這類 LLM 內建的嵌入矩陣。

cues.en: The table on this slide shows a brief overview of some of the characteristics of different embeddings matrices.
cues.zh: 這張表簡單整理不同嵌入矩陣的一些特性。

cues.en: In this and the next sections of the course, we will work with these four word two vec glove, gpt and Bert.
cues.zh: 這一章與下一章，會使用 Word2Vec、GloVe、GPT 與 BERT 這四種。

cues.en: And in later sections we will also look at a couple of different models.
cues.zh: 後面幾章，也會看幾個其他模型。

cues.en: Although the other models that we'll work with are pretty similar to GPT.
cues.zh: 不過，其他模型大致與 GPT 相似。

cues.en: Now when I use these words static and contextual here, this refers to the fact that word two vec and
cues.zh: 這裡的 static 與 contextual，也就是靜態與依上下文而變，指的是 Word2Vec 與

cues.en: glove embeddings don't change while you are working with them in the analyses.
cues.zh: GloVe 嵌入，在分析過程中不會改變。

cues.en: So once they are formed from the data, the vectors stay how they are.
cues.zh: 從資料建立後，向量就維持原樣。

cues.en: Large language models, on the other hand, actually take these embeddings vectors and modify them throughout the transformer architecture.
cues.zh: 另一方面，大型語言模型會取出嵌入向量，並在 Transformer 架構中持續修改。

cues.en: So as these vectors get passed from one layer to the next and one attention, head to the next.
cues.zh: 因此，這些向量從一層傳到下一層，從一個注意力頭傳到下一個時，

cues.en: Each of these vectors gets rotated and scaled a tiny bit, and that's what allows the models to flexibly
cues.zh: 都會略微旋轉與縮放，讓模型能靈活

cues.en: understand and generate text that is contextually relevant.
cues.zh: 理解並產生符合上下文的文字。

cues.en: These embeddings matrices are created in different ways.
cues.zh: 這些嵌入矩陣，建立方式不同。

cues.en: Towards the end of this section, I will show you how to create an embeddings matrix using a deep learning model.
cues.zh: 這一章最後，會示範用深度學習模型建立嵌入矩陣。

cues.en: It's not exactly how Word2 vec was created, but it's fairly similar to that method.
cues.zh: 並不完全等同 Word2Vec 的建立方式，但相當類似。

cues.en: The glove vectors are not based on neural networks and gradient descent, but instead are calculated
cues.zh: GloVe 向量不是以神經網路與梯度下降為基礎，而是根據

cues.en: Related, uh, based on, uh, word co-occurrences in text, and then applying some matrix factorization
cues.zh: 文字中單字的共同出現情況計算，再套用一些矩陣分解

cues.en: techniques to dimension reduce that very large co-occurrence matrices down to a smaller dimensional number of vectors.
cues.zh: 技巧，把非常大的共現矩陣，降到維度較小的向量表示。

cues.en: GPT and Bert have their embeddings matrices incorporated into the beginning of the language models.
cues.zh: GPT 與 BERT，則把嵌入矩陣放在語言模型的開頭。

cues.en: So the embeddings get trained along with the rest of the model according to methods and procedures that you will learn about later in the course.
cues.zh: 嵌入會和模型其他部分一起訓練，使用的方法與流程，課程稍後會學到。

cues.en: Now, the reason why we have different embeddings matrices is that people who study computational linguistics,
cues.zh: 之所以有不同嵌入矩陣，是因為研究計算語言學的人，

cues.en: or who work for companies that develop commercial applications of language models, have different requirements for what they want out of the embeddings vectors.
cues.zh: 或開發語言模型商業應用的公司，對嵌入向量有不同需求。

cues.en: For example, you can use these two embeddings matrices to study characteristics of words and semantic
cues.zh: 例如，可以使用這兩種嵌入矩陣，以量化方式研究不同文字中的單字特性與語意

cues.en: relationships in quantitative ways in different texts.
cues.zh: 關係。

cues.en: So these have a lot of research applications.
cues.zh: 因此，它們有很多研究用途。

cues.en: GPT is primarily designed for token generation and in particular next token prediction.
cues.zh: GPT 主要設計用於產生 token，尤其是預測下一個 token。

cues.en: So that actually changes the nature of the embeddings vectors in terms of how they are trained and how they are used.
cues.zh: 這會影響嵌入向量的性質，包括訓練與使用方式。

cues.en: And Bert is optimized for text classification and context comprehension.
cues.zh: BERT 則針對文字分類與上下文理解最佳化。

cues.en: Anyway, what you see here in this table is that different embeddings matrices can look different.
cues.zh: 總之，表中說明，不同嵌入矩陣，可能有不同樣貌，

cues.en: They can give different results from each other.
cues.zh: 可能產生不同結果，

cues.en: They have different targeted applications and so on.
cues.zh: 目標應用也不同，等等。

cues.en: Now I'm not going to get into a ton of detail about all these differences, but I want you to be aware that there is no such thing as the embeddings matrix.
cues.zh: 我不會深入所有差異，但希望你知道，並不存在唯一的「那個嵌入矩陣」。

cues.en: There are several different embeddings matrices, and the one that you use depends on the goal and the application.
cues.zh: 嵌入矩陣有很多種，要用哪個，取決於目標與應用。
